settings.form.effectiveWsUrlHint: WebSocket URL + Basic Auth below, as the charge point will dial it.
settings.form.soapHelpLocal: SOAP ChargePointService callback URL the Central System uses to reach this CP. Required only when using the daemon.
settings.form.soapHelpDerived: Leave empty to use the daemon's {{source}}: {{url}}
settings.form.soapHelpRequired: SOAP ChargePointService callback URL the Central System uses to reach this CP. Required.
settings.form.errSoapCallbackRequired: SOAP Callback URL is required in remote mode for SOAP versions.
settings.form.errProfile3Cert: Security profile 3 (mutual TLS) requires a client certificate and private key.
settings.form.derivedNote: derived from the {{source}} — the URL may change between daemon runs
settings.form.localSoapNoteBody: CP→CSMS calls (BootNotification, Authorize, etc.) work, but CSMS-initiated commands (RemoteStart, Reset, …) need the CLI/daemon which hosts the callback endpoint. The CSMS must allow CORS from this origin.
settings.form.authMtls: Authentication is governed by the mutual TLS client certificate and key in the Security section above (security profile 3).
settings.form.legacyBefore: Basic Authentication is currently active via the legacy Optional Settings toggle (username:
settings.form.legacyAfter: ). It will keep working unchanged. To manage authentication from the Security section instead, set Security Profile to 1 (Basic Auth) above and provide an Authorization Key — note the wire username becomes the Charge Point ID once you do, which may differ from the legacy username above.
settings.form.noAuth: No authentication configured. Set Security Profile to 1 above to enable Basic Authentication.
settings.form.authKeyGoverned: Authentication is governed by the Authorization Key in the Security section above (security profile {{profile}}).
settings.labels.help: Group charge points by site, tenant, environment… The dashboard filter and the cp.list API select on them.
settings.labels.errValueTooLong: Label “{{key}}” has a value that is too long.
settings.curve.minPoints: Must have at least 2 control points
settings.curve.title: Configure Auto MeterValue
settings.curve.canvasHint: Click to add control points, drag to move them
settings.curve.stopAtTarget: Charge until battery full (stop at EV's target SoC)
settings.curve.stopAtTargetHelp: Ignores the chart's max time/value. Uses EV Settings → Target SoC. Once reached, the in-flight transaction is stopped.
settings.page.title: Settings
settings.page.resetUnsupported: This runtime does not support state reset
settings.page.resetConfirm:
Reset all simulator data?

Scenarios, configuration overrides, charging profiles, availability flags, pending messages, logs and saved vehicle profiles will be erased. The page will reload afterwards.
settings.page.evSaved: Default EV settings saved. New connectors will start with these values.
settings.page.evReset: Default EV settings reset to the built-in defaults.
settings.page.invalidFile: Invalid JSON file. Please check the file format.
settings.page.invalidJson: Invalid JSON. Please check the syntax.
settings.page.runtimeModeBefore: The simulator picks Local or Remote automatically based on where the UI is served from. When opened via
settings.page.runtimeModeMid: (or the Docker image) the UI talks to that daemon as Remote; when opened from a static build (GitHub Pages,
settings.page.runtimeModeAfter: ) it runs the charge points in-browser as Local. No manual toggle.
settings.page.resetDataHelp: Wipe every persisted simulator record — scenarios, ChangeConfiguration overrides, charging profiles, availability flags, pending transaction messages, any saved logs and the saved vehicle profiles. Schema stays intact; the next load starts from a clean DB. In remote mode this also drops every charge point registered on the daemon.
settings.page.defaultEvHelp: These values seed every new connector's EV (battery capacity, target SoC, etc.) on this device. Scenarios that leave their "Scenario EV Settings" fields empty fall back to whatever the connector currently holds — which starts from this default.
settings.page.chargingCurveHelp: Battery-acceptance fraction of Max Power at each SoC. Empty (no points) means flat acceptance at Max Power for the whole session, matching the pre-curve behaviour.
settings.page.overrideActive: User override is active. New connectors will start from these values.
settings.page.noOverride: No override. New connectors start from the built-in Generic EV defaults (75 kWh / 80 % target).
settings.page.rfidHelp: Tag profiles shared across every charge point. Pick one from the connector card's TagID dropdown before Start Transaction. Stored globally — not per-CP.
settings.page.configMgmtHelp: Export your current configuration to a JSON file or import a previously saved configuration. You can also manually edit the JSON configuration below.
settings.page.jsonHelp: Edit the JSON configuration directly and click "Save" to update.
settings.page.note1: Individual charge point settings can be configured from the Home page
settings.page.note2: Click the gear icon next to each charge point tab to edit its settings
settings.page.note3: Use the "+ Add Charge Point" button to add new charge points
settings.page.note4: This page is for bulk configuration import/export only
